sections.content: How many people stayed in Wednesfield after gaining qualifications?

Wednesfield is a medium-sized town in the West Midlands. Wednesfield does not have its own university.

Wednesfield has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Wednesfield ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,235 state-school pupils from Wednesfield who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 350 (28%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 365 (30%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Wednesfield to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Wednesfield's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Wednesfield in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Wednesfield move to?

Of Wednesfield's graduates, 125 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 55 of those graduates (44%) were living fairly locally, in the Wolverhampton and Walsall travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Wednesfield's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 115 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 75 of those qualified non-graduates (65%) were living fairly locally, in the Wolverhampton and Walsall travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Wednesfield's GCSE cohort:

  • 45 graduates left the West Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 24% of graduates and 33% of qualified non-graduates living in Wednesfield had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 290 graduates and 365 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Wednesfield. This is compared with the 350 graduates and 365 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 76% of the graduates had also lived in Wednesfield as GCSE pupils, while 24% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Wednesfield in 2018 to 2019, 67% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 33% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
